name: CcsdsAttitudeQuaternion
description: A spacecraft attitude reported as a quaternion, transcribed from the Attitude Parameter Message the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems prints as an example in its Attitude Data Messages standard. The sample exists because four numbers between minus one and one are not an orientation until six independent conventions have been settled, and the message settles them in the text of the standard rather than in the record. Which frame the rotation starts from and which it ends at is fixed by the standard as running from `REF_FRAME_A` to `REF_FRAME_B`; whether the scalar is stored first or last is fixed by the standard as last; whether the rotation turns the body or turns the frame is stated only in an annex; and the handedness of the angle is stated nowhere. Read against the other choice of sense the same four numbers give the opposite rotation, and nothing in the payload objects. It demonstrates frameTransforms carrying a quaternion, `components` naming the scalar first while the record stores it last, and both frames written out as meta-types because the message identifies them by bare names drawn from a list in an annex rather than by any resolvable identifier.

object_name.description: Name of the spacecraft the attitude belongs to, from the `OBJECT_NAME` keyword of the message.

object_id.description: International designator of the spacecraft, from the `OBJECT_ID` keyword, in the launch-year and launch-number form the message uses, for example `1997-074A`.

originator.description: Organisation that produced the message, from the `ORIGINATOR` keyword. The standard does not require the originator to be the operator of the spacecraft.

creation_date.description: Time the message was produced, from the `CREATION_DATE` keyword. This is later than the epoch of the attitude it carries and is not a property of the attitude.

epoch.description: Time the attitude holds at, from the `EPOCH` keyword. The message states its time system in a keyword of its own and every time in the record is in that system; this record carries the value converted to UTC.

q1.description: First vector component of the attitude quaternion, equal to the first component of the rotation axis multiplied by the sine of half the rotation angle. The message prints this component first and the scalar last, and the annotation names the scalar first, because the annotation states meaning and the record states storage.

q2.description: Second vector component of the attitude quaternion, equal to the second component of the rotation axis multiplied by the sine of half the rotation angle.

q3.description: Third vector component of the attitude quaternion, equal to the third component of the rotation axis multiplied by the sine of half the rotation angle.

qc.description: Scalar component of the attitude quaternion, equal to the cosine of half the rotation angle. The standard that first carried these messages made the position of this component a field a producer filled in, taking the value `FIRST` or `LAST`; the current issue removed that field and fixed the position at last, recording the rationale as simplicity of the standard. The rotation angle it stands for is confined to a half turn either way whenever this value is not negative.

SpacecraftBodyFrame.name: SpacecraftBodyFrame
SpacecraftBodyFrame.description: The frame fixed to the spacecraft structure, named `SC_BODY_1` in the message. The standard lists the permitted frame names in an annex and gives no identifier that resolves to a definition, so the axes are written out here and cited by pointer. Which physical directions the three axes point in is a matter for the interface control document of the individual spacecraft, and the descriptions below record what such a document would state.

x.description: First body axis, along the boresight of the primary instrument.

y.description: Second body axis, completing a right-handed set with the other two.

z.description: Third body axis, along the nominal nadir direction of the spacecraft.

TerrestrialFrame.name: TerrestrialFrame
TerrestrialFrame.description: The Earth-fixed geocentric frame the attitude is reported against, named `ITRF1997` in the message. It is a realization of the international terrestrial reference system and is named in the message by that bare string, so it too is written out here rather than cited by URI. Writing it out records the axis order the components are indexed in, which the message does not state either.

x.description: From the geocentre towards the intersection of the equator and the reference meridian.

y.description: From the geocentre, completing a right-handed set with the other two.

z.description: From the geocentre towards the reference pole.
